task.description: Root-cause diagnosis (diagnosis only, not the fix) of ISS-0437: REQ-216's own requirement text describes per-tenant fair-share tracking against tenants that have made an admission attempt in a ROLLING WINDOW, but the shipped Letflow.Admission GenServer retains every tenant's entry in state.tenants indefinitely once created -- no time-decay/eviction mechanism at all. This was found and self-acknowledged by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR during REQ-216's own design gate (OQ-2), not silently missed. Two legitimate resolution paths are named in the issue, neither prescribed: (a) design and implement an actual rolling-window eviction mechanism for Letflow.Admission's per-tenant state, or (b) make an explicit decision that unbounded retention is PERMANENTLY acceptable given decision 0006's own tenant-cardinality bound, and correct REQ-216's design doc language to remove the stale rolling-window reference rather than leaving a requirement-vs-implementation mismatch on file. Read REQ-216's full requirement text in docs/requirements.yaml, the actual lib/letflow/design/req216-admission-control-core.md design doc (especially its own OQ-2 self-acknowledgment), the actual Letflow.Admission module's current state shape and tenant-entry lifecycle, and docs/migration/decisions/0006-*.md's tenant-cardinality bound, then recommend which of (a) or (b) is correct given the real operational stakes (how large can state.tenants actually grow in practice? is memory/lookup-time growth from unbounded tenant entries a genuine concern at decision 0006's stated tenant-count ceiling, or is it negligible?).
